title: A Humpback Closed Its Mouth Around Him

lines.text: One second he was diving for lobster. The next, everything went black.
Lobster diver Michael Packard was forty-five feet down.
But there were no teeth. No pain.
He was inside a whale's mouth.
Experts think a feeding humpback scooped him up by accident.
He still had his scuba tank, so he kept breathing.
He thought he was going to die. He thought of his sons.
But a humpback can't actually swallow a person.
Its throat is far too narrow.
After thirty to forty seconds, by his own estimate,
he saw light. The whale surfaced and threw its head side to side,
His crewmate, Josiah Mayo, pulled him from the water.
Bruised, sore, and no broken bones.
A humpback can't swallow you. But it can still close its mouth around you.

shots.environment: other:sandy seabed in green Cape Cod water (seabed builder, pale sand; low rocks; lobster as a small red-brown primitive prop)
shots.description: Mid-action from frame 1: diver close on the seabed, gloved hand reaching for a lobster by a rock; sun shafts above. At 55% of the shot a huge dark shape fills the top of frame and the image slams to black (only regulator bubbles faintly visible).
shots.camera: Close 28 mm over the diver's shoulder, slight push-in; on the blackout a 4-frame shake
characters: packard_diver (char_diver, single tank, black wetsuit, orange accent fins; stylised, faceless)
shots.lighting: Green daylight shafts (sun + caustics_light) then hard cut to near-black

shots.description: Map card: Cape Cod's hooked arm drawn as a stylised land shape curling up and left; the route line runs out along the arm to a pin just off its tip (Provincetown). Date stamp types in.
shots.camera: 2D card; slow zoom toward the pin

shots.description: Split-level view: a small lobster boat (new prop: 12 m white hull, small forward wheelhouse, open aft deck, low-poly) rocks on a sunny surface in the top third; the diver descends below it trailing bubbles to the sandy bottom. Name card + depth gauge in feet.
shots.camera: Wide 24 mm, camera at waterline then tilts down following the diver
characters: packard_diver (char_diver, single tank, black wetsuit, orange accent fins; stylised, faceless)
shots.lighting: Bright summer daylight above, green fade below; sun shafts

shots.description: Imagined beat: a grey shark silhouette (shark builder, 3.5 m) flashes past in the dark, lit only from below, then dissolves. Labelled as his thought, not what happened.
shots.camera: Fast lateral whip-pan 35 mm following the silhouette

shots.environment: other:inside the whale's mouth (near-black space; curved pale baleen 'curtain' of thin vertical plates suggested only by faint rim light; a slit of daylight where the lips meet)
shots.description: Darkness: the diver's silhouette, faint rim-lit, pats his own arms and legs, then reaches out and touches a smooth soft wall. Regulator bubbles drift but can't rise far (they pool against the 'ceiling').
shots.camera: Close 35 mm, slow push, very low exposure
characters: packard_diver (char_diver, single tank, black wetsuit, orange accent fins; stylised, faceless)
shots.lighting: Near-black; faint cold rim (area light 3 W) from an unseen gap

shots.description: Pull-back reveal: from the black, the camera rushes backward through the whale's closing lips into green daylight to reveal the whole humpback, jaws shut, throat grooves distended, the tiny diver's position marked by a soft glow inside the mouth (x-ray hint).
shots.camera: Fast dolly back 2 -> 25 m, 24 mm, ease-out; whale fills frame diagonally
characters: humpback (new prop built from primitives: ~12 m stretched-sphere body, dark slate top / pale throat, 8-10 ventral throat grooves as thin dark extruded strips, long white pectoral fins as flattened cones, fluke as two flattened wedges; lower jaw is a separate hinged object for open/close; knobbly head bumps as small spheres)
shots.lighting: Green daylight, sun shafts, caustics on the whale's back
fx: x-ray glow (emissive sphere inside mouth, 40% alpha)

shots.description: Wider replay of the lunge: a fish school swirls above the sand; the humpback rises from below at an angle, lower jaw dropping open, and engulfs the school and the diver in one sweep. THEORY badge.
